key_complications: thrombosis and paradoxically haemorrhage (acquired vWF deficiency at very high platelet counts)

biomarkers.name: JAK2 V617F
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnostic. JAK2-mutant ET carries higher thrombosis risk than CALR-mutant

biomarkers.name: CALR mutations (Type 1: 52-bp deletion; Type 2: 5-bp insertion)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Better thrombosis profile than JAK2-mutant ET. Type 1/type 1-like CALR is more often associated with myelofibrotic progression; type 2/type 2-like is more common in ET

biomarkers.name: Triple-negative (JAK2/CALR/MPL-negative)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Requires bone marrow biopsy for diagnosis; may have less favorable overall survival than driver-mutated ET in some series

biomarkers.name: IPSET / IPSET-thrombosis
biomarkers.clinical_use: Risk stratification for thrombosis (age, prior thrombosis, JAK2 status, cardiovascular risk factors)

biomarkers.name: ASXL1, SRSF2, EZH2, IDH1/2 (HMR mutations)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Adverse; not part of standard IPSET-thrombosis risk stratification. Adverse mutations have been incorporated into some mutation-enhanced prognostic models for ET

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Marrow megakaryocytic hyperplasia with large mature megakaryocytes and hyperlobated nuclei; loose clustering; no significant reticulin fibrosis (distinguishes from prefibrotic PMF)
variants: by driver: JAK2 (~50-60%), CALR (~20-30%), MPL (~3-5%), triple-negative (~10-15%)

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: As per other MPNs; inflammatory driver signalling
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Marrow megakaryocytic hyperplasia; distinguishing from prefibrotic PMF requires careful reticulin assessment and megakaryocyte morphology

cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Megakaryocytic hyperplasia with large mature megakaryocytes with hyperlobated nuclei; loose clustering; no significant reticulin fibrosis (distinguishes from prefibrotic PMF)
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Driver mutation biology reflects distinct JAK-STAT activation mechanisms: JAK2 V617F (~50-60%, direct kinase activation), CALR (~20-30%, mutant calreticulin activates thrombopoietin receptor MPL), MPL (~3-5%, thrombopoietin receptor mutations), triple-negative (~10-15%); all converge on JAK-STAT hyperactivation biased toward megakaryocytic lineage
